subject: space food
title: What If You Ate Dinner in Space?

scenes.text: What if you ate dinner in space? It would taste like you had a heavy cold.
In your first days in orbit, fluid that gravity kept in your legs drifts up into your head.
Your face puffs up and your nose blocks. Since smell drives flavour, your food goes flat.
In one astronaut's test, applesauce scored 6 out of 10 for taste on the ground, and only 4 in space.
So crews reach for hot sauce. One astronaut who disliked shrimp cocktail ate it constantly in orbit.
And forget bread. Floating crumbs can get into eyes and equipment, so since 1985 it's mostly tortillas.

description:
What if you ate dinner in space? Without gravity, body fluid shifts toward the head, causing a puffy face and blocked nose that feels like a heavy cold, so food tastes weaker; one astronaut rated applesauce 6 of 10 on Earth and 4 in space (NASA).
Crews add hot sauce and spicy condiments, and tortillas replaced crumb-shedding bread after 1985.
